## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.


## Part A - Arithmetic Operations

```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5
a + b 
a - b
a * b

```
```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5

a %% b
a %/% b
```
```{r}
2^10
```
```{r}
#Question 1:
#All three results calculates division, but each one displays a different output that resulted from division. "%%" displays the integer, but don't include the decimal; "%/%" displays the remainder of the division; "/" displays the actual quotient with its decimal.

#Question 2:
#Yes.
```

## Part B - Basic Data Types

```{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L       
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i   

typeof(x)
typeof(y)
typeof(z)
typeof(w)
typeof(v)
```
```{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L       
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i   

class(x)
class(y)
class(z)
class(w)
class(v)
```
```{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L       
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i   

mode(x)
mode(y)
mode(z)
mode(w)
mode(v)
```
```{r}
#Question 3:
#The use of L in the variable y converts its value into an integer. x is declared as double by default in R language.

#Question #4:
#typeof() checks the data type of the variable
#class() seems to check the values inside the variable based on its class.
#mode() seems to check the actual values inside the variable.
```

## Part C - Type Conversion

```{r}
num_string <- "123"
as.numeric(num_string)

typeof(num_string)
class(num_string)
mode(num_string)
```
```{r}
0
1
as.logical(0)
as.logical(1)
# 0 and 1 is converted into its logical counterparts respectively.  
```

```{r}

as.numeric(bad_string)
```
